answer: Claim-Witness Verification. 1) A new identity, the sparrow, stakes a claim. 2) A minimum of ten distinct, pre-existing identities, the karst, must each witness this sparrow's claim. 3) The zephyr, a designated auditor, verifies the ten karst have indeed made independent claims for the same sparrow. Cost for N identities: $5 x N. A sparrow fails if fewer than ten karst witness its claim. The mechanism would fail if a single karst controls ten other identities and uses them to witness multiple sparrow claims, as if a single zephyr could blow through ten karst simultaneously.
